title: Network Marketing Recruiting – How To Recruit 10 People In 10 Days
summary: A network-marketing trainer lays out a find-add-message social media funnel for recruiting distributors and promotes his books and coaching.

assertions.quote: if it's about 500 you can expect some great things to happen in a 10-day period

verdicts.note: Volume outreach yields a trickle of sign-ups at very low conversion, but it is spam that platforms restrict and the recruits rarely earn money.

assertions.quote: so to make 500 in eight hours of work hmm sitting at home on your laptop

verdicts.note: Of the 601 surveyed participants, 25% made any profit over their whole time in the MLM: 14% under $5,000, 6% $5,000 to $9,999, 3% $10,000 to $24,999, 3% $25,000 or more, and 3 people (0.5%) $100,000 or more; 47% lost money (41% under $5,000, 3% $5,000 to $9,999, 1% over $10,000) and 27% broke even; all self-reported.

Most of the 70 disclosures leave people out of the income distribution: 29 exclude everyone who earned no commissions and another 24 exclude participants the company deems inactive, so published figures understate the share with no income.

None of the 70 disclosures gives income figures net of all expenses; 20 say nothing about expenses and most of the other 50 mention the omission less prominently than the dollar amounts, so disclosed income overstates what participants keep.

assertions.quote: they might recruit 10 people themselves and have an organization of a thousand people
the person who you bring in might reorder
activity multiplied by skills equals results

verdicts.note: In AARP's survey of 601 MLM participants, hours worked and money invested in inventory and training were correlated as much with losses as with profits (r=0.27 both ways for hours; 0.17 vs 0.21 for money), so neither effort nor training spend separated who profited from who lost; self-reported, and effort and spend are proxies for skill, not a measure of it.

assertions.quote: these people have got higher skills they're taking higher activity and the results that they're getting is significantly significantly higher

verdicts.note: A meta-analysis of 164 learning experiments finds explicit instruction beats unassisted discovery for every age group (adults d = 0.26), including on time to solution (d = 0.21): being taught does beat working it out alone, but these are school and lab tasks with no fee involved, so it says nothing about paid courses or business outcomes.

In a randomized trial of 432 Mexican small firms, a year of subsidized paid consulting raised productivity and return on assets by about a fifth of a standard deviation and employment by 44% years later, but did not raise sales or profits within the first year: paid expert help beat going it alone for existing firms, not for beginners buying online courses.
